Definition: from G4491; to root (figuratively, become stable):--root.
BiblicalUsage: That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith, that ye, being rooted and grounded in love, may be able to comprehend, and as ye have received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk ye in Him, rooted and built up in Him, and stablished in the faith. The Greek text behind the King James Version gives the active verb, while the text I have checked gives the middle voice, ῥιζόομαι, the same rooting.
TheologicalSignificance: I am convinced that to be rooted is to be held fast where you are planted, and love is the soil.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
